summary: The panel showing the values under the pointer on a visx chart. visx positions it; this draws it.
useWhen: a chart drawn with visx shows exact values on hover
several series share an x value and the reader compares them at a point

useInstead.when: it explains a control rather than a data point
the reader needs every value, or needs them without a pointer

composition.note: Render it inside visx's Tooltip, TooltipWithBounds or TooltipInPortal with {...chartTooltipProps}, which turns off visx's own box so this one is the only panel. Axes take {...chartAxisProps} and gridlines {...chartGridProps}; a series takes className={chartSeriesClass(n)} plus ion-chart__line, __area, __bar or __point.
composition.example: <TooltipWithBounds top={top} left={left} {...chartTooltipProps}><ChartTooltip title="12 Sep" rows={[{ label: 'Success rate', value: '96.2%', series: 1 }]} /></TooltipWithBounds>

guarantees: rows are a <dl>, so each value is announced with its label
the series swatch is aria-hidden; the label carries the name
requires: a text summary and the values in a table (visually hidden is fine) — the tooltip appears on hover, so keyboard and screen-reader users never reach it
`value` already formatted — the tooltip cannot know the unit or precision

antiPatterns.dont: making the tooltip the only way to read a value
antiPatterns.why: it exists only under a mouse pointer; without a table the data is invisible to keyboard and screen-reader users

antiPatterns.dont: leaving visx's default tooltip styles on
antiPatterns.why: it draws a second white box with a hardcoded shadow around this one, and that box does not theme

antiPatterns.dont: a swatch colour that does not match the series
antiPatterns.why: pass the same `series` number the line or bar uses — the swatch reads the same token only if it is told the same index
